sigma/notice-0: Notice: a launch without a calculation is treated as a safety violation.
sigma/notice-1: Reminder: every error is entered in the protocol archive. The archive is kept indefinitely.
sigma/notice-2: Human Resources: interns without the introductory course are not admitted to the EMU-3 unit.
sigma/notice-3: Ventilation service: the noise in Sector B is normal. There is no cause for concern.
sigma/notice-4: Occupational safety: standing in the line of fire during a launch is prohibited.
sigma/notice-5: The administration thanks employees for their punctuality. Late arrivals are recorded.
classic/0-1: Master Karim placed a training tower in the field: "The stone from the tray flies exactly 30 paces. Place the tower so that it falls on the flag, and I will start teaching you seriously." Target: Hit the flag at the 52 m mark.
classic/0-2: The miller teases: "Bet you can't throw it to my flag?" John knows that the stone flies exactly two seconds. All that's left is to find the velocity. Target: Hit the flag at 36 m.
classic/0-3: Little sister Malika dropped an apple from the tower and asks: "How long was it flying?" John wants to answer before the apple falls again. Target: Predict the fall time with an accuracy of ±0.08 s.
classic/0-4: The shepherd asks to throw a bundle with lunch across the stream from the tower. Where will the bundle fall if thrown sideways? Target: Predict where the stone will land with an accuracy of ±1 m.
classic/0-5: Karim drew a triangle on the sand: "Forward twelve, up five. With what force to throw?" John remembers geometry lessons. Target: Find the launch speed by calculation and hit the flag.
classic/0-6: Now the other way around: the speed and angle are known. John needs to figure out how long the stone will stay in the air to have time to run to the target. Target: Predict the flight time with an accuracy of ±0.08 s.
classic/0-7: Storks are flying over the field. John doesn't want to hit them: how high will the stone rise? Target: Predict the apex height with an accuracy of ±0.8 m.
classic/0-8: Calculating on paper takes a long time. Karim brought an old counting box: "Teach it — and it will calculate for you". First program! Target: Complete the program so that the stone hits the flag at 34 m.
classic/0-9: There is an error in Karim's program — it crashes with an error. John fixes the function, and the counting box is back in business. Target: Fix fall_time so the stone from the 12 m tower flies 28 m from the tray (flag at 30 m).
classic/1-1: Master Karim's trebuchet is assembled! The first challenge is to hit a hay bale. The whole street gathered to watch. Target: Hit the hay bale at 66 m.
classic/1-2: Karim set the angle himself and squints slyly: "Where will it fall? Place the flag before the shot." Target: Predict the landing spot with an accuracy of ±6 m.
classic/1-3: The counting box is missing the target. John suspects that the machine is confusing degrees and radians. Target: Fix launch_velocity so the stone hits the bale at 73 m.
classic/1-4: Fairground challenge: three bales at different distances. The winner will get a honey cake! Target: Hit all three bales: 47, 62, and 71 m.
classic/2-1: A herald announced a throwers' competition in the large field. John wants to show the limit of the machine. Target: Throw it to the flag at 73 m (±1.5 m) — this is the machine's limit.
classic/2-2: The healer argues that the stone flies in an arc "like a rainbow". John wants to prove that it is a parabola and predict its vertex. Target: Predict the apex height with an accuracy of ±3 m.
classic/2-3: Karim asks to teach the counting box to calculate the entire flight, step by step. Target: Write step() so that the stone hits the flag at 73 m.
classic/2-4: A cart with pumpkins is rolling across the field — a festive target! Hitting a moving target is harder. Target: Hit the moving cart.
classic/3-1: In honor of the holiday — a training assault on an old fortress. The wall is far away, a heavy counterweight will be needed. Target: Hit the wall at 110 m.
classic/3-2: The villagers are arguing: twice as heavy — twice as far? John decides to check with a calculation. Target: Predict the landing spot with an accuracy of ±12 m.
classic/3-3: The beam was already cracking! Karim asks for a formula so as not to break the machine with a heavy counterweight. Target: Write beam_moment so that the master chooses a safe counterweight and hits the wall at 132 m.
classic/3-4: The finale of the assault: the gate and the tower. The audience held their breath. Target: Hit the gate and the tower.
classic/4-1: You need to pass a bag of tools across the gorge, but the wind is blowing against you. Target: Throw it to the target at 60 m (±1.5 m).
classic/4-2: A stone and a straw ball: what will the wind do to the light ball? John makes a prediction. Target: Predict the landing spot of the sphere with an accuracy of ±5 m.
classic/4-3: The counting box doesn't know about air. John is teaching it resistance. Target: Complete step() so that the stone lands on the target at 61 m.
classic/4-4: The old counting box calculates too infrequently, and the calculation "blows up". It needs to be made stable. Target: Make the calculation stable so the sphere lands on the target at 13 m.
classic/5-1: At night, John dreams he is on the Moon with his trebuchet. Where will the stone fall there? Target: Predict the landing spot with an accuracy of ±8 m.
classic/5-2: On the Moon, everything is slow, like in a dream. How many seconds will the stone stay in flight? Target: Predict the flight time with an accuracy of ±1 s.
classic/5-3: The counting box stubbornly calculates Earth's gravity. It needs to be taught about the Moon. Target: Fix step() so the stone lands on the target at 73 m.
classic/5-4: Lunar shooting gallery: a target rover drives through the dust. The last test of the dream! Target: Hit the moving target.
sigma/0-1: Directive No. 1: intern Doe is to complete the introductory course. The first exercise is to position the training tower so the projectile lands on the target mark. Task: Hit the target at the 52 m mark.
sigma/0-2: Lab assistant Kim set the flight time to 2 s and expects the initial velocity from the intern. A calculation error is grounds for a remark in the journal. Task: Hit the target at the 36 m mark.
sigma/0-3: To calibrate the stopwatches, the free fall time from the training tower is needed. The department awaits the number before the launch, not after. Task: Predict the fall time with an accuracy of ±0.08 s.
sigma/0-4: Horizontal launch from the tower: the projectile recovery team must occupy the impact point in advance. Specify it. Task: Predict the impact point with an accuracy of ±1 m.
sigma/0-5: Technical task: the projectile must launch with components of 12 and 5 m/s. Determine the total initial velocity using the Pythagorean theorem. Task: Determine the launch speed by calculation and hit the target.
sigma/0-6: The velocity and angle of the tray are known. The flight time is needed for the test range schedule — find the components using sine and cosine. Task: Predict the flight time with an accuracy of ±0.08 s.
sigma/0-7: Communication cables are stretched over the test range. Determine the height of the trajectory's apex so that the projectile passes under them. Task: Predict the apex height with an accuracy of ±0.8 m.
sigma/0-8: The intern is granted access to the department's computing machine. The first task is a program that calculates the launch speed itself. Task: Complete the program so that the projectile hits the target at 34 m.
sigma/0-9: There is a defect in the previous intern's program: division by zero. Fix the function and close the issue. Task: Fix fall_time so that the projectile from the 12 m tower hits the target at 30 m.
sigma/1-1: Clearance for the EMU-3 installation has been received. The first test is to hit the target stand at 66 m. Task: Hit the target stand at the 66 m mark.
sigma/1-2: The departure angle has been set by the supervisor. Your task is to specify the point of impact before launch. Task: Predict the impact point with a tolerance of ±6 m.
sigma/1-3: The speed calculation program is missing the target. Suspicion — confusion between degrees and radians. Task: Fix launch_velocity — the projectile must hit the target at the 73 m mark.
sigma/1-4: Control test: three targets at different distances, fewer launches — higher grade. Task: Hit all three targets: 47, 62, and 71 m.
sigma/2-1: Ground test range. Determine the release angle that gives the installation's maximum range. Task: Place the projectile at the 73 m mark (±1,5 m) — this is the limit of the installation.
sigma/2-2: Confirm the parabolic trajectory: predict the apex height before launch. Task: Predict the apex height with a tolerance of ±3 m.
sigma/2-3: A custom trajectory calculator is required: the step() function, step by step. Task: Write step() so the projectile lands at the 73 m mark.
sigma/2-4: A target cart is moving along the rails. Take its speed into account in your calculation. Task: Hit the moving target.
sigma/3-1: Destructive testing hangar. Select the counterweight mass so that the projectile reaches the target wall. Task: Hit the test wall at the 110 m mark.
sigma/3-2: Department hypothesis: doubling the counterweight doubles the range. Verify with a prediction. Task: Predict the impact point with a tolerance of ±12 m.
sigma/3-3: The beam's tensile strength is known. Write the moment calculation to choose a safe counterweight. Task: Write beam_moment so that the automaton chooses a safe mass and the projectile hits the wall at the 132 m mark.
sigma/3-4: Final sector test: hit the gate and the tower. Task: Hit the armored door and the column.
sigma/4-1: Aerodynamics hall: headwind. Adjust the release angle. Task: Place the projectile at the 60 m mark (±1,5 m).
sigma/4-2: Comparative test: steel projectile and light sphere. Predict the fall of the sphere. Task: Predict the impact point of the sphere with a tolerance of ±5 m.
sigma/4-3: Add air resistance to the calculator. Task: Complete step() so that the projectile lands on the 61 m mark.
sigma/4-4: The EVM-2 calculator calls step() rarely — the calculation is unstable. Fix it. Task: Make the calculation stable — the sphere must land on the 13 m mark.
sigma/5-1: Station "Sigma-L". First launch under lunar gravity: predict the point of impact. Task: Predict the landing spot with an accuracy of ±8 m.
sigma/5-2: Predict the flight time given g = 1,62 m/s². Task: Predict the flight time with an accuracy of ±1 s.
sigma/5-3: Earth's gravity is hardcoded in the calculator. Fix it. Task: Fix step() so that the projectile lands on the target at the 73 m mark.
sigma/5-4: Final station challenge: hit the moving rover target. Task: Hit the target on the lunar rover.
